bookStreet.title: Book Street Event Management System
bookStreet.summary: A system for booth rental, partner activities, registration and payments, with backend work focused on concurrent reservations and duplicate payment handling.
bookStreet.overview: I led a five-member team across 11 sprints and owned backend architecture, API contracts, ERDs and integration planning for the Book Street event system.
bookStreet.context: The project combined booth rental, partner activities, registration, authentication, payments and notifications. Concurrent reservations and repeated payment notifications were key engineering concerns.
bookStreet.responsibility1: Defined use cases, acceptance criteria, API contracts and ERDs; coordinated integration across the team.
bookStreet.responsibility2: Authored controller mappings for 127 of 188 REST endpoints and created 16 of 18 Flyway migrations.
bookStreet.responsibility3: Built Redis-backed session authentication and addressed reservation and payment concurrency.
bookStreet.architecture: The documented stack includes a Java/Spring Boot backend, PostgreSQL application schema, Redis-backed sessions, Flyway migrations, React, Docker and VNPay integration.
bookStreet.challenge1: Preventing conflicting outcomes when reservations are made concurrently.
bookStreet.challenge2: Handling duplicate payment notifications without repeating a business action.
bookStreet.decision1: Used pessimistic locking and UUID idempotency keys around concurrent reservation and payment flows.
bookStreet.decision2: Validated VNPay signatures and IPN notifications as part of payment handling.
bookStreet.results: The SQL scripts define 32 PostgreSQL application tables. The documented contribution covers 127 of 188 controller mappings and 16 of 18 Flyway migrations; these counts do not imply end-to-end ownership of every endpoint.
bookStreet.lessons: Engineering takeaway from the documented design: reservation state and payment retries need explicit concurrency and idempotency boundaries. A personal retrospective is still awaiting owner review.

moonCake.title: MoonCake E-Commerce System
moonCake.summary: A MoonCake commerce system with configurable gift boxes and batch-aware inventory, including checkout safeguards against duplicate orders and overselling.
moonCake.overview: I led a three-member team, designed the foundational SQL Server schema and coordinated integration for the MoonCake commerce system.
moonCake.context: The system covered customizable gift boxes, batch-based stock and checkout. Capacity limits, product expiry and stock restoration were documented constraints.
moonCake.responsibility1: Designed a foundational 19-table SQL Server schema and authored 14 of 20 Flyway migrations.
moonCake.responsibility2: Authored 64 of 93 Spring MVC handler mappings and coordinated full-stack integration.
moonCake.responsibility3: Developed gift-box capacity rules, FEFO allocation, expiry calculation and exact-batch stock restoration on cancellation.
moonCake.architecture: The documented stack includes Java 21, Spring Boot, Thymeleaf, SQL Server, Flyway, HTML/CSS/JS and VNPay. A verified full system diagram has not been supplied.
moonCake.challenge1: Avoiding duplicate checkout and overselling when stock changes concurrently.
moonCake.challenge2: Preserving batch-level stock and expiry rules across customization and cancellation.
moonCake.decision1: Used conditional state updates and pessimistic batch locking for checkout safety.
moonCake.decision2: Applied FEFO allocation, the earliest-expiring cake for box expiry, and exact-batch stock restoration after cancellation.
moonCake.results: The documented contribution includes a foundational 19-table schema, 14 of 20 Flyway migrations and 64 of 93 Spring MVC handler mappings. These are implementation counts, not measured production outcomes.
moonCake.lessons: Engineering takeaway from the documented design: batch identity matters when allocating and restoring stock; a total quantity alone cannot describe the cancellation path. A personal retrospective is still awaiting owner review.

DesignPreview.title: Glacial Precision
DesignPreview.description: A calm, cinematic system built from basalt-dark surfaces, bone typography, and measured glacial-blue interaction.

palette.title: A restrained spectrum
palette.description: Semantic roles keep the core palette consistent and let interaction states evolve without scattering raw color values.

typography.title: Editorial scale, technical clarity
typography.description: Space Grotesk carries display moments, Be Vietnam Pro keeps long-form reading balanced, and JetBrains Mono identifies technical metadata.
typography.bodySample: Clear hierarchy and generous rhythm keep the experience readable before any animation is introduced.
typography.supportingSample: Secondary context remains calm and legible.

components.title: A small, useful interface kit
components.description: Each primitive uses semantic HTML, visible focus, and shared interaction tokens.
components.surfaceBody: Borders carry most of the structure. Shadow and glow stay subtle enough to support, not dominate, the content.

layout.title: Space with a clear purpose
layout.description: The container expands from four mobile columns to six tablet columns and twelve desktop columns.
layout.copyWidth: Copy stays within a readable measure while the wider grid supports editorial compositions.

motion.title: Feedback before spectacle
motion.description: P1 uses lightweight CSS transitions only. System reduced-motion preferences collapse decorative movement and shorten feedback.
